land.text: the palatial state of Mycenae with Tiryns and Nauplion: 'two to three times the size of the other palatial states' (40 km disc, 5,027 km2)

successors.note: 'Mycenae was among the numerous Aegean sites destroyed as part of the Bronze Age Collapse around 1200 BC'; 'culminated in the destruction of Mycenae itself c. 1150 BC'; 'partly rebuilt'; 'the site remained sparsely populated until the Hellenistic era'. The land passed to no state. (eu-01-a's mycenaean-greece dossier moves the seat to Tiryns in 1190.)

capitals.name: Mycenae
capitals.note: 'Situated in the north-east corner of the Argive plain'; the palace dates only 'to the start of LHIIIA:2'. Tiryns as a second seat after the destruction is eu-01-a's reading.

correction.text: Mycenae and the Argive plain (20 km disc round Mycenae, 1,257 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws the Peloponnese as one Mycenaean shape. 'Mycenae developed into a major power during LHI (c. 1550 - c. 1450 BC)'; shaft-grave evidence for Minoan influence 'from c. 1600 BC'. The page gives no area; a 20 km disc is the researcher's reading of the Argive plain.

correction.text: the palatial state of Mycenae with Tiryns and Nauplion: 'two to three times the size of the other palatial states' (40 km disc, 5,027 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'At its peak in 1350 BC, the citadel and lower town had a population of 30,000 and an area of 32 hectares'; 'The palace of Mycenae probably ruled over a territory two to three times the size of the other palatial states' (the Pylos page: 2,000 km2, so 4,000-6,000 km2 for Mycenae); 'Its territory would have also included adjacent centers, including Tiryns and Nauplion'. The 40 km disc is 5,027 km2.

ledger.note: c. 1550: Mycenae becomes a major power. 'Mycenae developed into a major power during LHI (c. 1550 - c. 1450 BC)'; the shaft graves show 'extensive Cretan influence (Minoan) in the region from c. 1600 BC'. The land (the Argive plain) is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: c. 1350: the palatial state at its peak includes the adjacent centres. 'Its territory would have also included adjacent centers, including Tiryns and Nauplion'; the page gives no date for their incorporation (1350 is the page's peak year, a bridge).

region.text: the palatial state of Mycenae with Tiryns and Nauplion: 'two to three times the size of the other palatial states' (40 km disc, 5,027 km2)

ledger.note: c. 1150: Mycenae destroyed. 'Mycenae was among the numerous Aegean sites destroyed as part of the Bronze Age Collapse around 1200 BC' and the collapse 'culminated in the destruction of Mycenae itself c. 1150 BC'; the causes are 'unknown' (enemy attack, internal strife, earthquakes). The page gives both 1200 and 1150.

certainty.note: No boundary is known; the territory is a disc of the size the page implies.

sources.title: Mycenae
sources.note: LHI major power, 1350 peak, territory two to three times the other palatial states, Tiryns and Nauplion, destruction c. 1200/1150, Argos 468.

notes: A palace state inside Cliopatria's Mycenaean Greece (-1500..-1101, eu-01-a); the renderer should carve it from that shape. The page gives no km2, so the size is derived from 'two to three times the size of the other palatial states' with the Pylos page's 2,000 km2 (5,027 km2 for the 40 km disc); both pages are Wikipedia. The destruction: c. 1200 for the Aegean collapse, c. 1150 for Mycenae itself (the page does not reconcile them; eu-01-a has 1190). The page's 'Built: c. 2100 BC' in the infobox is unexplained; the page does not mention Midea. After 1150 the site is sparsely populated until the Hellenistic era; Argos captured Mycenae in 468 BC (Archaic section) and razed it: a possible later event for a gap filler (Argos is a counterpart needing a dossier). Related: kingdom-of-pylos, mycenaean-greece, greek-dark-ages.
